kind: method sketch (Morning Brief 2026-11-23, Track C, pick #1); not a reproduction

source.citation_title: KeyMem: Temporal Occupancy Control for Robust Streaming VideoLLM Memory
source.authors_as_listed: Wei Song, Yuxin Cao, Xiao Cheng, Christy Jie Liang, Xi Zheng, Leo Yu Zhang
source.repository: none listed on the abstract page
source.use: method only, paraphrased: fixed-duration time buckets with a hard per-bucket slot cap over a bounded memory; the optional secret-key sampler, rank normalisation of base scores and every model component are left out

declared_choices_not_from_the_paper: rank order (score, t, id): lower score leaves first, then the older item, then the smaller id
when the whole memory is over capacity, the most crowded bucket gives up its lowest-ranked item; a tie among equally crowded buckets goes to the lowest-ranked of their lowest items
the recency arm (plain FIFO with global capacity only) as a second weak baseline
the gate: a planted burst must crowd out an earlier needed item under score_only while bucket_cap holds the cap and every needed item

measured.note: counts of synthetic planted cases, not rates; they say nothing about video models

mutants.rule: a timed-out mutant is reported TIMEOUT and is never counted as a kill

on_unmeasured.what: author-reported: 20 s of burned-in captions occupy 84% of an 8 s memory and lower accuracy over all clips from 79.4% to 58.3% (Qwen2.5-VL-7B)
author-reported: temporal quotas raise the worst accuracy of attention-based retention at the smaller budget from 42.2% to 73.3-76.1%
the paper's optional secret-key sampling of survivors and its behaviour under an adaptive adversary; not implemented
rank normalisation of an arbitrary base score; fixture scores are already one integer scale
visual tokens, frames, attention scores or any model; items here are synthetic village notes
how to pick bucket_seconds and bucket_cap for a real village memory; fixtures declare them
